5. Processing your applications

Some payments are quicker to process than others. To make sure we get money to you as quickly as possible we pay each element as soon as it is ready. This means you are likely to receive multiple payments from us.

We use the information you provide in your application. It’s important you complete your application as accurately as possible so that we pay you the correct amount.

We expect to make payments for redundancy pay, holiday pay and arrears of pay within 6 weeks of receiving your complete application, and information from the insolvency practitioner. We will contact you if we need you to provide any further information so that we can pay your claim.

To allow us to deal with everyone’s application as quickly as possible, do not contact us to check the status of your application until 6 weeks have passed.

If you’re a director of a company, the Insolvency Service will contact you before the 6 weeks to ask for extra information.

6. Next steps

Because you’ve been made redundant, it’s important you apply for employment related benefits such as Universal Credit and New Style Jobseeker’s Allowance.

Use the benefits calculator to find out what benefits you might be entitled to.

When you apply for benefits, keep any letters, or take screenshots of the acceptance or rejection that confirms what you are eligible for.

Later, when we calculate your loss of notice payment, we have to subtract the amount of employment based benefits you were eligible to receive during your notice period. We do this even if you did not apply for either benefit.

We will require evidence if you are rejected for these benefits.

Contact us with a copy of the rejection letter from the job centre or a screenshot of your online application.

7. Protective awards

If your employer did not consult you before you were made redundant, you may be entitled to a compensation payment called a protective award. To get a protective award, you will need to make a claim to an employment tribunal.

We have further guidance explaining more about protective awards.

8. Getting help

If you have any questions, contact the insolvency practitioner dealing with your case.

You can also read further information about our redundancy payments process.

If you’re a director check our guidance to help you know your employment status and rights.

9. Information we collect about you

We collect data about you from the insolvency practitioner dealing with your employer’s insolvency. This may include personal data. We process this information even if you decide not to go ahead with your redundancy claim.

You can find details of how The Insolvency Service treats your personal information in our personal information charter.
